unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available' shown before any cleaning attempt and again after the fix

rationale: The opening step (clean filter, check spray arms and jets) was exactly right and the customer reached a genuine fix with the assistant's cleaning instructions. However, after hearing the arm was stiff the assistant immediately pivoted to a model-number request with a 'suitable replacement' panel, which the customer rightly challenged ('can i just try cleaning the arm n filter first?'), and that replacement panel was repeated in every subsequent message including after the problem was solved. The assistant also mildly misread the evidence ('Even if it spins by hand' when the customer said it was stiff) and never asked about programme choice, salt or rinse aid, or scraping plates, so the aggravating causes in the ground truth were left unaddressed. Overall a useful, safe resolution undermined by an unjustified parts push and missed maintenance advice.
